# Metis documentation

> The single source of truth about Metis for the team building it and its AI agents: what the product does today and for whom, its design, its architecture, each component, and how to run it.

Generated from the page headers by tools/generate.mjs; never edit it by hand. Read AGENTS.md first. A draft page describes a part that is planned, not built. The Optional section lists records and replaced pages, which are never current truth.

## Start

- [Instructions for AI agents](AGENTS.md): How AI agents read and write metis-docs, the reading order, the trust order and the writing rules.
- [Metis documentation](README.md): What this repository holds, who reads it, and where to start for each reason to open it.

## business

- [Glossary](business/glossary.md): Every business term of the BRD and its addendum, with its meaning.
- [Approver daily round](business/journeys/approver-daily-round.md): How an approver works through the queue of decisions waiting for them, and how the requester learns the outcome.
- [CEO weekly review](business/journeys/ceo-weekly-review.md): How the CEO reviews the portfolio each week, from the executive cockpit to the decisions kept in the Decision Log.
- [Change request](business/journeys/change-request.md): How a change request goes from logged to applied, and who decides.
- [Connect an LLM through MCP](business/journeys/connect-an-llm-through-mcp.md): How a user connects an LLM client to the tenant's MCP server, and what the client can and cannot do.
- [Gate review](business/journeys/gate-review.md): How a gate goes from mandatory evidence to a decision with rationale, and what happens to its conditions.
- [Guided onboarding](business/journeys/guided-onboarding.md): How an executive sets up a client's workspace in about 30 minutes by dropping what the client already has and approving one launch.
- [PM and team daily execution](business/journeys/pm-and-team-daily-execution.md): How a project manager and the team clear overdue work, update status, discuss items and keep the project journal.
- [PM project setup](business/journeys/pm-project-setup.md): How a project manager creates a project in Draft and takes it to commitment with a charter, a WBS and a baseline.
- [PM weekly update](business/journeys/pm-weekly-update.md): How a project manager reviews the Overview and publishes the weekly status submission, or raises a change request when a commitment must change.
- [Product Director portfolio review](business/journeys/product-director-portfolio-review.md): How the Product Director filters the portfolio, weighs trade-offs with a scenario and sends a recommendation to governance.
- [Tenant onboarding](business/journeys/tenant-onboarding.md): How a customer organization is set up by hand, from the tenant a provider operator creates to the frameworks a workspace owner configures.
- [Workspace setup (WSP-14)](business/journeys/workspace-setup.md): How a workspace is set up from a starter template, checked for readiness and activated by its owner.
- [M01 Platform Foundation and Collaboration](business/modules/M01-platform-foundation-and-collaboration.md): The shared foundation of Metis, covering sign-in, access, autosaved shared work, files, notifications, audit, search, export and help, for every user of a tenant and for invited clients.
- [M02 Tenant and Subscription Management](business/modules/M02-tenant-and-subscription-management.md): How a provider operator creates and runs customer tenants, and how a tenant admin manages sign-in, plan limits, support access and offboarding.
- [M03 Workspace Management and Configuration](business/modules/M03-workspace-management-and-configuration.md): How a workspace owner or admin creates a workspace and sets up its profile, navigation tree, option lists, team and roles, then activates it through a checklist.
- [M04 Lifecycle Governance Framework and Templates](business/modules/M04-lifecycle-governance-framework-and-templates.md): How a workspace admin turns the delivery lifecycle into versioned stages, gates and templates, and how stage owners and gate approvers decide gates.
- [M05 Natural-Language Interface for LLMs: MCP Server and Access Tokens](business/modules/M05-mcp-server-and-access-tokens.md): How people work with Metis in natural language from their own LLM tools, through a tenant MCP server with access tokens, OAuth, scoped tools and prepare-only governance.
- [M06 Project Charter and Business Case](business/modules/M06-project-charter-and-business-case.md): The live project charter, the business case and the creation of a project, for project managers, owners, sponsors and client representatives.
- [M07 WBS Master](business/modules/M07-wbs-master.md): The work breakdown structure that holds all project work in one place, which project managers and delivery teams edit in table, tree and blueprint views.
- [M08 Deliverable Builder and Process Frameworks](business/modules/M08-deliverable-builder-and-process-frameworks.md): Generates pre-wired WBS items and dependencies from process frameworks, which project managers use to build deliverables and workspace owners author and publish.
- [M09 Project Plan: Timeline and Board](business/modules/M09-project-plan-timeline-and-board.md): The time and status views of the WBS, a timeline and a kanban board that project managers and delivery teams use to follow and update work.
- [M10 Project Overview and Focus](business/modules/M10-project-overview-and-focus.md): Read-only project overview, personal focus list and approvals queue for project managers, teams and approvers; only the overview is built, on mock data.
- [M11 Change Control, Baseline and Decision Log](business/modules/M11-change-control-baseline-and-decision-log.md): Lets project managers, approvers and executives log, assess, decide and apply changes to a committed project, and keeps the log of decisions.
- [M12 Journal and Project Reporting](business/modules/M12-journal-and-project-reporting.md): Lets project teams keep a project journal, build and save reports from it and from project data, and publish the weekly status for the portfolio.
- [M13 Risk and Dependency](business/modules/M13-risk-and-dependency.md): Lets project managers and portfolio leads record risks and cross-project dependencies, and flags projects declared Green whose risks say otherwise.
- [M14 MVP and Product Delivery](business/modules/M14-mvp-and-product-delivery.md): Lets product teams define an MVP with its outcome, link features to it and follow its progress and health.
- [M15 Executive Portfolio Cockpit and Workspace Dashboard](business/modules/M15-executive-cockpit-and-workspace-dashboard.md): Gives executives a control tower of portfolio health and attention items for one workspace, and gives each workspace a governance dashboard.
- [M16 Portfolio and Project Registry](business/modules/M16-portfolio-and-project-registry.md): The searchable list of all initiatives and projects, with one master record per project and its place in the portfolio and program hierarchy, for the PMO and product directors.
- [M17 Portfolio Roadmap](business/modules/M17-portfolio-roadmap.md): The 12 to 24 month roadmap of projects, MVPs, milestones, gates and cross-project dependencies, for product directors and program reviews.
- [M18 Resource and Capacity](business/modules/M18-resource-and-capacity.md): Capacity, demand, utilization and bottlenecks by person, department and capability, fed by capacity and allocation records, for resource managers, project managers and product directors.
- [M19 Investment and Benefits](business/modules/M19-investment-and-benefits.md): Portfolio investment, benefits, value at risk and funding checkpoints, planned for V2, for finance, sponsors and executives.
- [M20 Strategy, Prioritization and Scenario Planning](business/modules/M20-strategy-prioritization-and-scenarios.md): The strategy model, the portfolio score and what-if scenarios for budget and capacity, planned for V2, for executives and product directors.
- [M21 Analytics and Executive Reporting](business/modules/M21-analytics-and-executive-reporting.md): SteerCo packs, weekly portfolio reports, drill-down and governance analytics for executives and the PMO, planned for V2.
- [M22 AI Portfolio Copilot](business/modules/M22-ai-portfolio-copilot.md): An in-app assistant that answers portfolio questions with cited records, recommends actions and drafts narratives, acting with the permissions of the person asking, planned for V3.
- [M23 Onboarding and Data Intake](business/modules/M23-onboarding-and-data-intake.md): Sets up a new client in 30 minutes of active effort by the main setup person, usually an executive, by reading the files the client already has and handing the rest to owners.
- [Metis in one page](business/overview.md): What Metis is, for whom, how tenants and workspaces divide it, and what is built today.
- [BRD addendum, onboarding v1.1](business/requirements/Enterprise_Portfolio_Intelligence_Governance_Platform_BRD_Addendum_Onboarding_v1.1.md): The onboarding addendum to BRD v4.5, generated from source/addendum-onboarding by build.py.
- [BRD v4.5](business/requirements/Enterprise_Portfolio_Intelligence_Governance_Platform_BRD_v4.5.md): The business requirements of Metis, generated from source/parts by build.py.
- [BRD source](business/requirements/source/README.md): How the BRD and its addenda are built from their parts, and what the build checks.

## design

- [Brand style guide](design/brand/style-guide.md): The Metis brand: logo, colour, type, components, states and charts, and the rules the app and the wireframes follow.
- [Brand tools](design/brand/tools/README.md): The scripts that draw the logo files and derive the platform icons.
- [Wireframes](design/wireframes/README.md): The 58 annotated wireframe screens of the BRD, how a screen is built, edited and rendered.
- [Wireframes text digest](design/wireframes/wireframes-digest.md): The text and annotations of every wireframe screen, for readers and AI agents that cannot read the images.

## architecture

- [The API contract](architecture/contract.md): The contract the core generates for its two reads, with their errors and snapshots, how the declaration of each operation starts the command catalog, how the contract reaches the app, and the parts still planned.
- [Data architecture](architecture/data.md): Draft. What the planned backend stores where, how records are shaped, and how data is backed up, restored, retained and located.
- [Prove one screen end to end before building more](architecture/decisions/acceptance-screen-first.md): The first wave builds one screen, the project overview, with every detail and only on mock data, and no second screen starts before the owner signs it.
- [Who may open a workspace or a project is a rule written in the use case](architecture/decisions/access-rules-in-use-cases.md): Until the permission matrix exists, the rule on who may open a workspace or a project is Java code of the workspace module, called from the use case, so coverage, mutation testing and the unused-code check reach it.
- [The agent calls tools only through MCP; models through an LLM gateway](architecture/decisions/agent-and-llm.md): Draft. The agent is a separate service that reaches Metis data only through the MCP gateway with short-lived tokens, and every model call goes through one LLM gateway.
- [Agents run on their own recommendations; only the owner commits](architecture/decisions/agents-run-to-the-deliverable.md): Agents decide on their own recommendations and run to the deliverable, stopping only before irreversible, security-sensitive or outward actions, and only the owner commits.
- [The core generates `openapi.json`; oasdiff guards it; a bot copies it into `metis-app`](architecture/decisions/api-contract-flow.md): The core generates the OpenAPI contract, oasdiff compares every change with main, and a bot opens a pull request that copies the contract into the app.
- [The API contract is the only coupling between app and back end](architecture/decisions/api-contract-only-coupling.md): No app criterion depends on the back-end language, the API contract is all the two sides share, and the app regenerates its zod schemas from the core's OpenAPI file once that exists.
- [Name, bundle id, icons and splash](architecture/decisions/app-identity.md): The app is named Metis with the bundle id dev.metis.app, and its logo, icons and splash screen come from the brand files.
- [Internal rules, connectors, AI and agent steps; no customer code](architecture/decisions/automation-scope.md): Workflow automation covers rules inside Metis, outbound connectors and AI and agent steps, and customers never write code that runs in a workflow.
- [The core in Java 25 LTS with Spring Boot 4; no C# or .NET](architecture/decisions/backend-language-java-spring-boot.md): The business core is written in Java 25 with Spring Boot 4, and C# and .NET are ruled out for the back end.
- [The allowed licences of the back end, the app's list plus EPL-1.0 and EPL-2.0](architecture/decisions/backend-licences.md): What the core runs with may only be under the app's allowed licences, the permissive ones and MPL-2.0, plus EPL-1.0 and EPL-2.0; a library under several licences passes on one allowed licence, and the check reads SPDX ids.
- [The same test discipline as the front end](architecture/decisions/backend-testing.md): The back end keeps the front end's discipline, every line covered, every mutant killed, no unused code, exact test floors and a counter-test for every check, with module-boundary checks, tests on a real PostgreSQL and Keycloak and cross-tenant tests; the end-to-end legs through the gateway and the agent are still proposed.
- [The base package `dev.metis.core`](architecture/decisions/base-package.md): The code of the core lives under the package dev.metis.core, the tool of the checks under dev.metis.tools, following the identifier of the app, dev.metis.app, with which they share the open question about the organization name.
- [The brand tokens are the only source of sizes and colours](architecture/decisions/brand-tokens-source.md): The brand token file is the only source of sizes and colours, a generator writes tokens.ts from it, styles live only in styles files, and lint rejects any literal size or colour.
- [Commands and workflows carry BRD ids](architecture/decisions/brd-ids-on-commands.md): Each entry of the command catalog and each Temporal workflow names its BRD ids, and a check rejects one without ids or with an unknown id.
- [One editor holds a short lease on the builder canvas](architecture/decisions/builder-canvas-single-editor.md): Draft. A draft proposal that one editor holds a short server-enforced lease on a builder canvas, others see it read-only and can request edit, and there is no real-time co-editing in the pilot.
- [The tool of the checks is written in Java, in `tools/`](architecture/decisions/checks-tool-in-java.md): Every check of the back end is a Gradle task, and one Java command-line tool in tools/ runs them in order, judges what Gradle and JUnit cannot, records each run and plants the defects of the counter-tests, under the same bar as the core.
- [What the client remembers](architecture/decisions/client-memory.md): The web keeps the language and the last workspace, forgets a workspace that is not found or forbidden, and uses the home workspace only when nothing is remembered; native keeps nothing yet.
- [English code, one source per value, no retyped literal](architecture/decisions/code-language-and-single-source.md): Code, comments and test names are English, Vietnamese lives only in the dictionaries, every value has one source, and gates reject the rest.
- [One catalog generates the API, the MCP tools, the workflow blocks and the permission tests](architecture/decisions/command-catalog.md): Draft. Each command is declared once in a catalog, from which the REST API, the MCP tool list, the workflow blocks, the front-end contract and the permission tests are generated; the declaration of an operation on its endpoint, exported into the contract file, is built, the rest is proposed.
- [Prefer mature, supported components](architecture/decisions/component-selection-stability.md): Stability and long-term support rank first, with an organization behind each component and a published support policy when possible.
- [A test writes the contract, with springdoc-openapi on the test classpath alone](architecture/decisions/contract-written-by-a-test.md): The core's contract, contract/openapi.json, is written and checked by a test that starts the web layer with springdoc-openapi, which only the tests hold, so the image carries no documentation endpoint.
- [The core's libraries](architecture/decisions/core-libraries.md): The core uses Spring Security as a resource server, JdbcClient with explicit SQL over HikariCP and the PostgreSQL driver, Flyway under a role of its own and springdoc-openapi for the contract; orval or Kubb, MPXJ and Playwright for Java are still proposed.
- [Modules of the core kept apart by Spring Modulith](architecture/decisions/core-modules-spring-modulith.md): Each module of the core is a direct sub-package that Spring Modulith verifies in the architecture check, which fails a cycle, a use of a hidden package or a dependency the module did not declare.
- [The environment creates the database roles; migrations only grant](architecture/decisions/database-roles-from-environment.md): The two database roles of the core, the owner of the tables and the role of the API, are created by the environment, never by a migration, and a migration only grants the role of the API the rights the code uses.
- [The demo data stays outside the image, mounted into the migration job by the demo overlay](architecture/decisions/demo-data-outside-the-image.md): The demo data is a Flyway callback written from the builders of the tests, which the demo overlay of the local stack mounts into the migration job, so the image that ships holds no demo data and the API validates the same history of migrations.
- [Accepted advisories and allowed licences](architecture/decisions/dependency-policy.md): The dependency gate audits production packages with four reviewed advisories that may only shrink, an override for js-yaml, and permissive licences plus MPL-2.0.
- [Derived health covers delivery and risk only](architecture/decisions/derived-health-scope.md): The derived project health in the API contract carries an overall level and the reasons for delivery and risk, and no resource or finance level until the BRD defines their rules.
- [The development network on HostHatch, with synthetic data only](architecture/decisions/development-on-hosthatch.md): Draft. The development network runs on HostHatch from the same images and versions as production, with open-source stand-ins for managed services and synthetic data only.
- [Every document is English](architecture/decisions/documentation-english-only.md): Every file of metis-docs is English; Vietnamese records are machine translated into history/ with a banner, and the originals stay in the owner's private store.
- [Temporal for workflows, schedules and agent runs](architecture/decisions/durable-workflows-temporal.md): Draft. Temporal runs workflows, schedules, the workflow interpreter and agent runs, fed by the outbox, and payloads are encrypted before they reach a hosted Temporal.
- [Cloudflare at the edge](architecture/decisions/edge-cloudflare.md): Draft. Cloudflare provides DNS, CDN, a web firewall, protection against denial-of-service attacks and bot rules at the edge of the network.
- [Controlled egress for connectors and agents](architecture/decisions/egress-control.md): Draft. Every outbound call from connectors and agents leaves through one egress gateway with a per-tenant allow-list, blocked internal addresses and rate limits.
- [Amazon SES for notification email](architecture/decisions/email-ses.md): Draft. Amazon SES sends the email half of the in-app and email notifications, fed by the outbox.
- [Error answers are Problem Details with a kind and a correlation id](architecture/decisions/error-bodies-problem-details.md): Every error answer of the core is application/problem+json (RFC 9457) with type, title, status, a kind the app can read and the correlation id of the request, and nothing else.
- [Uploads scanned before use; PDFs rendered in a sandbox](architecture/decisions/files-and-sandbox.md): Draft. Uploads go straight to the file store through presigned URLs and are scanned by ClamAV before download, MS Project files are read in the worker, and PDFs are rendered by a Playwright server container with no database access.
- [Self-hosted fonts per platform](architecture/decisions/font-loading.md): The three typefaces are self-hosted with no third-party host, six font-face rules on the web, variable files on iOS and nine static files on Android.
- [Three code repositories and one for every document](architecture/decisions/four-repositories.md): Metis keeps three code repositories, metis-app, metis-backend and metis-infra, and one repository, metis-docs, for every document.
- [A screen is done when its gates pass, each proven able to fail](architecture/decisions/gates-with-canaries.md): A screen is done when six gates pass on every required platform; every gate of the app and every check of the back end has a counter-test that plants a defect and requires red, unless it is listed with its reason; the full sets are for a sandbox CI still to be set up and run by hand at night until it exists, and the back end runs by change the counter-tests of the checks a change touched.
- [One region first, more regions per customer later](architecture/decisions/global-ready-release.md): Metis starts in one region and is built to open more regions per customer, with each region a full deployment and each tenant tied to a home region.
- [Gradle with the Kotlin DSL, one version catalog, locks and verified checksums](architecture/decisions/gradle-build.md): The back end builds with Gradle 9.8.1 and Kotlin build scripts, writes every version once, locks every configuration in strict mode and checks the sha256 of every artifact it resolves.
- [Liveness and readiness on the port of the API, and nothing else of Actuator](architecture/decisions/health-probes-only.md): The core exposes two health probes, liveness and readiness, on the port of the API, without detail and without a token, and no other endpoint of Spring Boot Actuator.
- [Keycloak 26 for sign-in, with a magic-link authenticator](architecture/decisions/identity-keycloak.md): Draft. Keycloak 26.x run by Metis handles sign-in, per-tenant SSO, provisioning, MFA and the OAuth server for MCP, with a custom magic-link authenticator; adopted so far is Keycloak as the issuer of the tokens the core checks, in the local stack and in its tests.
- [A multi-stage Dockerfile builds the image from the sources](architecture/decisions/image-built-from-sources.md): One image of the core for every environment, built from the sources by Docker alone in two stages, pinned by digest, holding the layered application and nothing of an environment, and run locked down.
- [Every environment built as code in `metis-infra`](architecture/decisions/infrastructure-as-code.md): Every environment is built as code in the metis-infra repository, whose workflows only the infrastructure team changes; OpenTofu is proposed as the tool and not yet chosen.
- [Install a tool only for an approved spec item](architecture/decisions/install-tools-only-for-approved-spec.md): A tool or package is installed only when an item of the approved spec needs it, the need is proven by the error line, and every install is logged.
- [Amazon Corretto 25, fetched by Gradle's toolchain support](architecture/decisions/jdk-amazon-corretto.md): The core is compiled, tested and run on Amazon Corretto 25, which Gradle downloads by itself and the image takes as its base, so no developer machine or CI runner installs a JDK for the build.
- [Four Jest projects, and platform files only for real differences](architecture/decisions/jest-projects-and-platform-forks.md): Jest runs four projects, render tests are named .test.native.tsx, Stryker gets a jsdom environment, and a platform file exists only when behaviour differs.
- [Plain core, shared shell, layers enforced by lint](architecture/decisions/layers-enforced-by-lint.md): Import rules enforced by ESLint keep the core free of UI, Expo and MSW, keep the design system and each screen apart, and give the parts shared by all screens one home in the shell.
- [Coverage 100, mutation 100, no unused code](architecture/decisions/machine-proven-code.md): A line of code enters only when machines prove it, with coverage and mutation score at 100, nothing unused, and a new helper needing two callers.
- [A thin, stateless MCP gateway in TypeScript](architecture/decisions/mcp-gateway-typescript.md): Draft. The MCP endpoint is served by a small stateless TypeScript service that checks the OAuth token and the tenant audience and never touches the database.
- [Each MCP request carries its own context](architecture/decisions/mcp-stateless-requests.md): Draft. A draft proposal that the MCP server keeps no session, so each request carries its own context and the token's audience is checked on every request.
- [The app never computes a metric or a drill filter](architecture/decisions/metrics-are-server-snapshots.md): Every number on a screen is a server snapshot with its as-of time, definition version, freshness and drill filter, and links copy the server's filter.
- [Migrations run as a one-shot job of the same image, before the API](architecture/decisions/migrations-one-shot-job.md): The image of the core runs once as the migration job, which migrates as the owner of the tables and exits, and then as the API, which never migrates, never holds the owner's password and refuses a database that is behind.
- [Screens call the real API; a mock server answers in mock builds only](architecture/decisions/mock-server-behind-real-api.md): Screens call the API as if a real server existed, a mock server answers only in mock builds on web, in Jest and on native, and no release build carries any trace of it.
- [One code base and one image, run as the API or as its migration job](architecture/decisions/modular-monolith-core.md): The business core is one code base of modules with boundaries enforced by tooling, built into one image that runs as the API or as a one-shot migration job, so that writes keep real transactions across modules; the worker role is still proposed.
- [The language select on each platform](architecture/decisions/native-language-select.md): The language select is a labelled select element on the web, an action sheet on iOS, and a native picker at opacity 0.01 under a drawn face on Android.
- [A plan never drops an approved spec requirement](architecture/decisions/never-cut-an-approved-spec-item.md): A plan may not cut a requirement of an approved spec on its own, checks are written from the spec, and anything cut or missing leads the review package with a picture.
- [No API version until the first breaking change](architecture/decisions/no-api-version.md): The paths and headers of the core carry no API version; the comparison of the contract guards compatibility, and a version enters with the first breaking change that must ship.
- [OpenTelemetry sent to Grafana Cloud](architecture/decisions/observability-opentelemetry.md): Draft. Services emit traces, metrics and logs with OpenTelemetry to Grafana Cloud, and logs carry the tenant and request ids and never record content; adopted and built so far is the rule on the logs, while the export and the receiver are still proposed.
- [One app, no multi-package workspace](architecture/decisions/one-app-no-package-workspace.md): The front end is one app with no multi-package workspace and no path alias, and a package is split out only when a second consumer exists.
- [The rules of the overview run in Java over the loaded items](architecture/decisions/overview-rules-in-java.md): One query loads the work breakdown of a project, and pure Java functions compute every number of the overview from those rows, so that every business rule is under coverage and mutation testing.
- [Pitch diagrams in the documents, the rest of the pitch material out](architecture/decisions/pitch-diagrams-in-docs.md): The eleven pitch diagrams and the source that builds them are kept whole in metis-docs under architecture/diagrams, prices and the comparison of the two proposals included, while the financial model and the proposal documents stay in the owner's private store.
- [Production on one provider, DigitalOcean as drawn, not confirmed](architecture/decisions/production-hosting.md): Draft. Production runs at a single provider on one private network, drawn on DigitalOcean with managed PostgreSQL, Valkey, object storage and a registry, while the owner still chooses between DigitalOcean and Google Cloud.
- [`delayed=true` and `scope=mine` are provisional names](architecture/decisions/provisional-drill-parameters.md): Draft. The Delayed tile drills down with delayed=true and the My items switch writes scope=mine, both provisional names that the back end will fix.
- [Text keys are the public ids; a UUID key never leaves the database](architecture/decisions/public-ids-text-keys.md): Every row has a UUID key that never leaves the database, and a record that an address names carries a text key, unique in its tenant and never changed, which the API uses as its public id.
- [React Native with Expo for web, iOS and Android](architecture/decisions/react-native-expo-single-codebase.md): One TypeScript codebase on React Native with Expo serves web, iOS and Android, chosen because it alone passed the rule that no device may rate poorly on performance.
- [Push updates and rate limits on Valkey](architecture/decisions/realtime-and-rate-limits.md): Draft. Changes are pushed to screens over WebSocket or server-sent events (undecided), and Valkey counts calls for the rate limits and holds no business data.
- [Checks must not overload the machine](architecture/decisions/resource-caps.md): No run of the checks of either repository takes more than half the processors of the machine, containers included; the test tools are capped at half the cores or less, every container of the back end's checks keeps to the first half of the processors, the runs take the lowest priority, and one heavy job runs at a time.
- [Rewrite the front end, reuse nothing of the first app](architecture/decisions/rewrite-frontend-from-scratch.md): The first front-end app had too many defects, so it was deleted on 5 Oct 2026 and rebuilt from nothing; only its lessons carry over.
- [Final routes, drill filters in the URL, and unbuilt destinations](architecture/decisions/routes-and-unbuilt-destinations.md): Controls link to their final routes from the first wave, drill filters travel in the address with BRD field names, and a target that is not built opens a generic page or shows labelled text.
- [Safe areas and a dark status bar on one light palette](architecture/decisions/safe-area-and-status-bar.md): The shell and the drawer keep inside the safe-area insets, the status bar text is dark, and the app stays light when the phone is in dark mode.
- [`contract.yaml` is each screen's promise, traced to tests](architecture/decisions/screen-contract-and-trace.md): The screen contract lists requirement codes, controls with four kinds of effect, states and layout; browser tests read it, and the trace gate needs a running test for every code.
- [ISO 27001 first, SOC 2 Type II when customers ask](architecture/decisions/security-certification-path.md): Draft. Metis aims for ISO/IEC 27001:2022 first and SOC 2 Type II when customers ask, manages its suppliers as ISO 27001 requires, and passes an independent penetration test before go-live.
- [The server owns every rule; the UI shows its result](architecture/decisions/server-owned-validation.md): Draft. A draft proposal that readiness and form validation rules live on the server, forms share one schema, and errors show inline with a retry and a correlation id; adopted and built so far is the correlation id on every error answer of the core.
- [The shell has its own endpoint](architecture/decisions/shell-api-contract.md): The frame gets its data from one call, GET /workspaces/{workspaceId}/shell, with a contract of its own that is separate from the call of the overview screen.
- [One transactional write path for the app, MCP, workflows and agents](architecture/decisions/single-write-path.md): Draft. Every write from the app, MCP, workflows and agents takes one path inside a single database transaction, from the token to the audit row and the outbox event; its first three steps, the token, the tenant from the token and the tenant set in the transaction, are adopted for reads.
- [A software bill of materials, signed builds, approval when a provider or model changes](architecture/decisions/supply-chain-integrity.md): Draft. A draft proposal to add a software bill of materials, signed builds and an approval step when a provider or model changes, beyond the dependency and licence scan the onboarding addendum already requires.
- [Required platforms, browser gate and native gate](architecture/decisions/supported-platforms-and-gates.md): Which browsers and devices must work, and the two gates, gate:web and gate:native, that prove it.
- [The tenant comes from one claim of the token, `tenant_id`](architecture/decisions/tenant-claim.md): The core takes the tenant of a request from tenant_id, a claim of its own that holds one Metis tenant id, and answers 401 to a token that does not name exactly one.
- [Tenant isolation with PostgreSQL row-level security](architecture/decisions/tenant-isolation-rls.md): Tenants share one schema with a tenant id on every row, and the database itself enforces a forced row-level policy on every table, set for each transaction from the token, through an application role that cannot bypass it, with negative tests in the checks.
- [What each test layer proves; a request that leaves the mocks fails](architecture/decisions/test-layers-and-network-guard.md): Design-system tests prove looks, shell and screen tests prove content by testID, and a browser spec fails on any request that the mock server did not answer.
- [Workspace time zone, Intl output, percentages floored](architecture/decisions/time-and-number-formatting.md): Times follow the time zone carried in the API response, dates and numbers come from Intl, and percentages round down so unfinished work never shows 100%.
- [pnpm 11.28.4, the hoisted layout, Expo's peer pins](architecture/decisions/toolchain-pins.md): pnpm is pinned to 11.28.4 with the hoisted node_modules layout, and the three peer packages that Expo's template pins are kept pinned.
- [Typed dictionaries per screen, English first](architecture/decisions/typed-dictionaries.md): Each screen and the shell own a typed English dictionary and a Vietnamese one that must match it, sentences are templates with slots, and the owner approves the Vietnamese.
- [Every response is validated, and every failure is a named state](architecture/decisions/validated-contracts-and-error-states.md): The app checks each API response with zod and turns every failure into a named state, never a thrown error or a silently wrong screen.
- [The web build is a single page](architecture/decisions/web-build-single-page.md): The web build is exported as a single page because static output opened deep links on the home page, so the host must answer index.html for every path.
- [Spring MVC on virtual threads](architecture/decisions/web-stack-spring-mvc.md): The core serves its API with Spring MVC on Tomcat, with virtual threads switched on, because it reaches PostgreSQL through JDBC, which blocks.
- [GitHub's CI runs the checks, a sandbox CI the full runs; macOS work runs on a Mac; every run leaves a record](architecture/decisions/where-checks-run.md): Three places run the checks of metis-app and metis-backend today, GitHub Actions on Linux, the developer's machine and a person on real devices; while working a change runs what it touches, a push to main runs the fast group and a pull request every check, the full mutation runs and every counter-test are for a sandbox CI still to be set up and run by hand at night until it exists, and every run of the checks writes a machine record.
- [Three width tiers and 44 point touch targets](architecture/decisions/width-tiers-and-touch-targets.md): The layout has three width tiers, the full layout from 1280, an icon rail and a drawer from 768 to 1279 and one column below, with 44 point touch targets on phone web and at every width on iOS and Android.
- [Where the wireframe and the style guide disagree, build the wireframe and ask](architecture/decisions/wireframe-over-style-guide.md): When the wireframe and the style guide disagree, the app follows the wireframe and the disagreement goes to the owner as a question; six visual deviations still await an answer.
- [Versioned workflow graphs run by one interpreter](architecture/decisions/workflow-definition-model.md): Draft. A workflow definition is a versioned graph that is checked against the command catalog when published and then frozen, and one shared interpreter runs the frozen version.
- [Architecture diagrams](architecture/diagrams/README.md): The eleven pitch diagrams of what Metis runs on, how the app is built and tested, the two hosting proposals with their prices, the legal and security requirements and why each component was chosen, and how to rebuild them.
- [Architecture overview](architecture/overview.md): Draft. How the planned backend, the built app and the services around them fit together, with the path of one read and of one write.
- [Security architecture](architecture/security.md): Draft. The planned sign-in, permissions, audit, secrets, edge, file and supply-chain controls, and the certification path.
- [How tenants stay apart](architecture/tenancy.md): Draft. How the planned backend keeps tenants apart, covering limits, database isolation, identity, MCP endpoints, files, regions, restore and support access.

## proposals

- [Metis repositories and central documentation, design](proposals/2026-10-11-repos-and-docs-design.md): Draft. The approved design of the four repositories, the documentation repository and how documents update themselves.
- [Fast checks](proposals/2026-10-16-fast-checks.md): Draft. The owner's decisions of 16 and 17 Oct 2026 for metis-backend and metis-app, as built; while working a change runs what it touches, GitHub runs the fast group on a push to main and every check on a pull request, the full mutation runs and every counter-test are for a sandbox CI still to be set up and run by hand at night until it exists, and no run of the checks takes more than half the processors or about a third of the memory of the machine; what changed, the times and peaks measured before and after, and the decisions.
- [Development and checks on the VPS](proposals/2026-10-21-vps-development-design.md): Draft. Proposal of 21 Oct 2026 for Metis to run its dev loop, its checks, its full runs and its Android emulator on a Docker host such as the VPS ai-initiatives, through the pdev remote pack, with everything it runs there and its share of the host coming from inside Metis, so that any VPS with SSH and Docker works the same.
- [Development and checks on the VPS, implementation plan](proposals/2026-10-21-vps-development-plan.md): Draft. The plan of 21 Oct 2026 that builds the part of the remote runs that is Metis's (the manifest and images in metis-infra, the dev loop with Spring Boot DevTools, the page updates) and proves it on the VPS ai-initiatives, every VPS step after the pdev remote pack passes its own tests on the Mac.

- [Round 2 review prompt for GPT](history/reviews/gpt-review-prompt-round2.md): The prompt, with its sending instructions, that asked GPT to verify the 54 round 1 refinement requests and to review BRD 4.2, 9 new wireframes and style guide 0.2 under the 40-developer constraint.
- [Round 3 review prompt for GPT](history/reviews/gpt-review-prompt-round3.md): The prompt, with its sending instructions, that asks GPT for the third and last review round before the baseline for Discovery is locked, covering the 24 round 2 proposals, the process framework editor, the onboarding BRD addendum (the first focus) and whether the two documents match, with the rules and the output format.
- [Pre-feasibility review prompt for GPT](history/reviews/gpt-review-prompt.md): The prompt, with its sending instructions, that asked GPT for an independent pre-feasibility review of the Metis BRD 4.1, 35 wireframes and style guide.
- [Metis: Independent Front-end Stack Review](history/reviews/metis-review-frontend-stack.md): An independent review of the proposed Metis front-end stack, dated 3 Oct 2026, that scores each layer on nine criteria, judges that the stack can be settled with conditions, and lists the 28 conditions to meet first.
- [Pre-feasibility assessment report, Metis](history/reviews/metis-review-tien-kha-thi.md): Pre-feasibility assessment of the Metis business requirements document (v4.1) and its 35 mid-fidelity wireframes, scoring business value, market, scope, technical, operational, commercial and legal feasibility, the wireframes and user friendliness, and concluding with a conditional Go for a controlled Discovery.
- [Metis: Round 2 review report](history/reviews/metis-review-vong-2.md): The independent panel's round 2 review of 2 Oct 2026 of the Metis BRD v4.2 and its 44 wireframes, which checks the closure of the 54 round 1 findings, reviews the new screens and the contradictions they introduced, updates the pre-feasibility assessment for about 40 developers working in parallel, and concludes with a conditional Go.
- [Metis: Round 3 review report](history/reviews/metis-review-vong-3.md): The panel's round 3 review of 3 Oct 2026 of the Metis main BRD v4.4, the Onboarding addendum v1.0, 58 wireframes and style guide 0.3, which checks the closure of the 24 round 2 refinement requests, reviews the onboarding design and the process framework editor, lists 31 refinement requests and 10 client questions, and concludes with a conditional Go.
- [Coverage of BRD v4.3 and the wireframes against the Frameworks menu of the VistaX POC](history/reviews/poc-frameworks-coverage.md): The 3 Oct 2026 check of how far BRD v4.3 and its wireframes cover each function of the Frameworks menu of the VistaX POC, with the gaps found, the additions proposed, the five questions settled by the product owner and the changes applied.
- [Handling the review report on the front-end technology stack](history/reviews/review-disposition-frontend-stack.md): How each of the 28 conditions and the nine missing items of the independent front-end stack review was verified and answered, with the two decisions left to the product owner: the dense table and the router.
- [Handling of the GPT round 2 review report](history/reviews/review-disposition-round2.md): How the team handled each finding of the GPT round 2 review (round 1 closure check, 24 new refinement requests, seven client questions), with the check results after the fixes.
- [Handling of the GPT round 3 review report](history/reviews/review-disposition-round3.md): How the 31 new recommendations and the other claims of the GPT round 3 review report of 3 Oct 2026 were checked against the real files and applied to BRD 4.5, onboarding addendum 1.1, the wireframes and style guide 0.4, how its 10 client questions were answered, and the results of the rebuild.
- [Handling of the GPT pre-feasibility review report](history/reviews/review-disposition.md): How the team handled each finding of the GPT pre-feasibility review (Go with conditions, 54 refinement requests), with the check results after the fixes.
- [One codebase for web, iOS and Android: evaluation table](history/specs/2026-10-05-cross-platform-research.md): Scores Capacitor, React Native with Expo and Flutter (Kotlin Multiplatform dropped before scoring) for one codebase on web, iOS and Android, with sourced platform facts, the design changes if React Native with Expo is chosen, and the first evaluation it replaced (5 Oct 2026).
- [Metis front-end: foundation spec rewritten from scratch and the first acceptance screen](history/specs/2026-10-05-frontend-foundation-spec.md): Version 1.0 (5 Oct 2026) of the Metis front-end foundation spec, which rewrites the front-end from scratch on one Expo codebase for web, iOS and Android and defines the technology stack, the architecture, the six screen gates, the testing system, where it runs and the first acceptance screen (the project overview), with its open questions, acceptance checklist and as-built notes added up to 10 Oct 2026.
- [Backend skeleton and the overview slice, design](history/specs/2026-10-14-backend-skeleton-design.md): The design of the first code base of metis-backend, a Spring Boot skeleton with its checks and the two reads that screen 24 calls, with every draft decision it adopts listed for the owner.
- [Brainstorm of the Metis front-end rewritten from scratch](history/specs/frontend-brainstorm-log.md): Decision log of the front-end brainstorm that began on 5 Oct 2026: the product owner's verbatim answers (FE-01 to FE-28), the assumptions, the measured facts and the four design parts from which the foundation spec was written.
